analysis.body:
# US Grid Interconnection Queues: September 2026 Snapshot

Across five major grid operators, 8,374 generation and storage projects totaling 1.33 million megawatts are in various stages of interconnection requests—a queue backlog that reflects sustained demand for reliable power supply. ERCOT dominates by volume at 438,086 MW across 1,778 projects, followed by NYISO at 319,115 MW and MISO at 299,721 MW. Storage has become a major component of this pipeline, with 326,231 MW queued across ERCOT, MISO, and SPP combined, suggesting grid operators and developers are responding to the need for flexibility and firming capacity alongside variable renewable sources.

Gas generation still represents a substantial portion of planned interconnections—184,345 MW across all five operators—but has been outpaced by solar, which totals 265,861 MW in the combined queues. This shift accelerates when storage is included as a carbon-displacement enabler rather than a fuel source. Wind adds another 169,464 MW across ERCOT, MISO, and SPP. The diversity of fuel types in active development indicates utilities are not betting on a single technology path, a posture consistent with meeting both firm baseload expectations and the variability introduced by concentrated, high-utilization data center loads.

Commercial-sector electricity sales across eight key states reached 54,797 MWh in June 2026, with Texas reporting the highest absolute volume at 15,754 MWh and California second at 10,025 MWh. California's commercial rates average $27.33 per MWh compared to Texas's $8.66, a 3.2-fold spread that reflects transmission constraints, renewable curtailment costs, and grid management complexity—factors that directly shape data center site selection and power purchase agreement negotiations. Watch for the next ERCOT quarterly report to see whether gas and storage allocations shift further or whether solar capacity orders plateau as interconnection lead times extend.
